item.title: China, Pakistan hold high-altitude army drills with Beijing-supplied arms
item.description: In a landmark move, China and Pakistan have kicked off their inaugural joint military exercise, dubbed Karakoram 2026, in the high-altitude region of Xinjiang. This operation emphasizes counter-terrorism strategies, utilizing advanced Chinese military technology. The participating forces aim to refine their skills in mountainous terrains, thus fortifying the strategic partnership between the two nations. The exercise promises improved synergy as troops navigate shared operational standards.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: ‘Big items are done’: Envoy Gor hints major boost in India-US trade negotiations
item.description: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor confirmed that negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement are advancing rapidly. Both sides have resolved major issues and are close to finalizing the agreement. Gor emphasized that the pace of negotiations is unusually swift compared to previous trade deals. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar also indicated that progress ensures a positive outcome is imminent.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: After 50 years of fighting, Austin may secure Muny’s 141 acres while UT develops 190 acres nearby
item.description: Austin residents have passionately defended the historic Lions Municipal Golf Course for years, opposing potential developers. A new proposal seeks to officially hand over ownership of the golf course to the city, safeguarding its future. In return, the University of Texas would gain revised development regulations for neighboring properties on Lake Austin Boulevard. Officials assert that this arrangement effectively balances the need for green spaces with urban expansion.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Van Gogh’s hidden 1890 masterpiece resurfaces after 60 years, with a $180 million auction estimate
item.description: Vincent van Gogh's exquisite painting, Châtaigniers en fleurs, has resurfaced after being tucked away for over sixty years and will soon hit the auction block in New York. With an estimated value of around $180 million, this piece could shatter records. Once acquired in 1975, it has remained within the Blaquier family collection, drawing excitement from collectors, particularly during the recent preview in Hong Kong.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2013, friends launched RXBAR with $10,000; Kellogg bought it for $600 million four years later
item.description: In 2013, aspiring entrepreneurs Peter Rahal and Jared Smith launched RXBAR while searching for nutritious protein bars. Starting from Rahal's parents' basement, they sold directly to customers. Their venture gained tremendous traction, culminating in a $600 million acquisition by the Kellogg Company in 2017, highlighting a significant trend towards clean-label snacks. Rahal remained CEO for two years post-acquisition before transitioning out.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US temple attack plot: Teen’s alleged manifesto describes Indians as ‘subhumans’
item.description: A 19-year-old white supremacist's intention to attack a temple near Chicago was disrupted by a rifle malfunction. Following the incident, concerned colleagues notified authorities after he expressed his intentions via messages. Police arrested Alexandros Paporakis, uncovering alarming materials including a manifesto that targeted several communities. The case has raised serious safety concerns among Hindu organizations about worship places.

item.title: US not to livestream execution of Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan
item.description: Former US Army Major Nidal Hasan is scheduled for execution by firing squad on December 3, for the 2009 shooting at the US Army's Fort Hood base in Texas. Donald Trump stated that the execution will not be livestreamed, despite previous announcements from the Pentagon. Howevr, immediate family members of the victims may attend in person, if they choose.
item.dc:creator: Karan Manral

item.title: Brazil plants 840,000 trees to restore 607 hectares of Atlantic Forest
item.description: Brazil's Atlantic Forest is undergoing remarkable restoration efforts, spearheaded by World Land Trust and Reserva Ecológica de Guapiaçu. With 840,000 trees planted over 20 years, 607 hectares of degraded land have been revived into verdant forest. This initiative has created a vital wildlife corridor, facilitating the return of over 220 bird species to the previous wetland, while striving to protect and enhance the Guapiaçu watershed's remaining forest.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: France begins implementing agreement to protect Saudi oil facilities; what it means
item.description: France has started deploying military resources to Saudi Arabia to protect its oil facilities from regional attacks. This decision follows an agreement aimed at enhancing defense cooperation, especially amid increased drone and missile threats. President Emmanuel Macron confirmed the deployment, which includes soldiers and defense systems to bolster security. Recent attacks by Houthi militants have escalated tensions in the area, raising concerns for energy stability.

item.title: Bought in 2014, Magnolia’s Waco site grew from to 5.3 acres, adding shops, a ball field and church
item.description: In a remarkable transformation, Chip and Joanna Gaines have converted a historic cottonseed mill site in Waco into a buzzing tourist hub. Spanning 5.3 acres, the revitalized Magnolia property now features an array of shops, dining venues, and lush green spaces. Guests can experience restored historic buildings like the Old Church, while the newly built Katy Ballpark commemorates the original Katy Park.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Gabriella Rothberg, 17, who turned a sandwich idea into a patent for meat-flavoured tomatoes
item.description: A sandwich idea at 15 led Miami student Gabriella Rothberg to develop genetically engineered tomatoes designed to produce heme, an iron-containing molecule associated with meat flavour. Now 17, she is listed alongside her father on a US patent issued in June 2026. The project remains experimental, with taste and nutritional benefits yet to be established.

item.title: Police shooting, water shortages, rising costs: Mauritius extends curfew amid unrest
item.description: Mauritius has extended a curfew for two additional nights after protests erupted over police violence. The unrest followed the shooting of a woman by a police officer in Camp Levieux, prompting increased tensions. Authorities reported over 100 arrests related to the disturbances and canceled school classes for security reasons. Anger over rising living costs and worsening water shortages has fueled public discontent across the island.
